questions.question: If sinθ = (4)/(5), Find the value of sin3θ
questions.solution:
**Given:**

sinθ = 4/5 

**Formula Used:**

sin3θ = 3sinθ - 4sin³θ 

**Calculation:**

sin3θ = 3sinθ - 4sin3θ 

⇒ sin3θ = 3(4/5) - 4(4/5)³

⇒ sin3θ = 12/5 - 256/125

⇒ sin3θ = 44/125 

**∴ The answer is 44/125.**

⇒ x = 228 × 3/2 = 342 

 20% of the number = (20/100) × 342 = 68.4 

**∴ 20% of the number is 68.4.**

questions.question: What is the area of a triangle whose sides measure 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The side of the triangle is 5, 6 and 7 cm 

**Formula Used:**

Area of triangle = √[s(s - a)(s - b)(s-c)], where s = semiperimeter of the triangle 

Semiperimeter (S) = (1/2) × Sum of sides of the triangle

**Calculation:**

Semiperimeter (s) = (a + b + c)/2 = (5 + 6 + 7)/2 = 9

⇒ Area of the triangle = √[s(s - a)(s - b)(s-c)]

⇒ √[9(9 - 5)(9 - 6)(9 - 7)] = √(9 × 4 × 3 × 2) = 14.69 cm² 

**∴ the area of the triangle is 14.69 cm2**

questions.question: If the height of an equilateral triangle is 12 cm, then what is the area of the triangle?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Height of the equilateral triangle = 12 cm 

**Formula Used:**

Height of triangle = (√3/2) × side of an equilateral triangle 

Area of an equilateral triangle = (√3/4) × side²

**Calculation:**

Side of the triangle = (2/√3) × 12 = 8√3 

Area of the triangle = (√3/4) × (8√3)² 

⇒ (√3/4) × 64 × 3 = √3 × 16 × 3 = 48√3 cm²

**∴ The area of equilateral triangle is 48√3 cm² **

 

**Traditional Method**

 

Height = 12 cm

Height = √3/2 × Side

12 = √3/2 × Side

Side = 24/√3 cm

Area of Eq Triangle = √3/4 × Side2

Area of Eq Triangle = (√3/4) × (24/√3) × (24/√3)

⇒ 6 × 24/√3 

Now 6 can be written as 2 × √3 × √3

⇒ 2 × √3 × √3 × 24/√3 = 48√3 cm2

questions.question: A product, whose MRP is Rs 978 , is sold for Rs 925 by a wholesale shop owner. What is the percentage of discount given by him?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Discount Percentage** = (**Discount** ÷ **MRP**) × 100

**Discount** = 978 − 925 = 53

**Discount %** = (53 ÷ 978) × 100 ≈ 5.4%

**∴ The correct answer is 5.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**MRP (Marked Price)** = ₹978

**SP (Selling Price)** = ₹925

**Formula Used:**

**Discount** = **MRP** − **Selling Price**

**Discount %** = (**Discount** / **MRP**) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4d8234c23654a6581b41ada40e47f112ba9c987330ed40ae54268e78556f15b1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Discount Amount** = 978 − 925 = 53

⇒ **Discount %** = (53 ÷ 978) × 100

⇒ **Discount %** = 5300 ÷ 978

⇒ **Discount %** ≈ 5.419%

**∴ The correct answer is 5.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MRP)

The price printed on the product label, also known as the **List Price** or **Tag Price**. Discounts are always calculated on this value.

Successive Discounts

When two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the **Effective Discount** = (d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100)%.

Profit/Loss Base

While **Discount** is calculated on **Marked Price**, **Profit** or **Loss** is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**.

questions.question: Two cars start from the same place at the same time at right angles to each other. Their speeds are 72 km/hr and 54 km/hr, respectively. After 20 seconds the distance between them will be:
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Speed of 1st car = 72 km/hr 

speed of 2nd car = 54 km/hr

**Formula Used: **

x km/hr = x × (5/18) m/s 

Distance = time × speed

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e73fcd03ecc0179aec2bfd250f727ed4e100da28dfe32255dc184d1cd0c19f2.png] 

The speed of the 1st car = 72 km/hr = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s 

⇒ The distance "AB" travelled by car in 20 seconds is = 20 × 20 = 400 m

The speed of the 2nd car = 54 km/hr = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s

⇒ The distance "BC" travelled by car in 20 seconds is = 15 × 20 = 300 m

Since two cars are moving at right angles to each other, so we will apply the Pythagoras theorem to find the distance between them.

The distance "AC" between them after 20 seconds is, √(AB² + BC²) 

⇒√(400² + 300²) 

⇒ √25000 

⇒ 500 m 

**∴ After 20 seconds the distance between them will be 500 m.**

questions.question: The ratio of tables and chairs in a room is 7 : 9. If there are 560 tables and chairs in the room, then what is the number of chairs ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of ratio parts = 7 + 9 = 16 units

Total items given = 560

1 unit = 560 ÷ 16 = 35

Number of **chairs** (9 units) = 9 × 35 = 315

**∴ The correct answer is 315 chairs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of **tables** to **chairs** = 7 : 9. Total **tables and chairs** = 560.

**Formula Used:** Value of a part = (Ratio of part ÷ Sum of ratios) × Total Value

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/821e0d4501357b019586b9435cd65355d90424d5ae22d02c4cb342aa1e24375f.png] 

⇒ Let the number of **tables** be 7x and **chairs** be 9x.

⇒ 7x + 9x = 560

⇒ 16x = 560

⇒ x = 560 ÷ 16 = 35

⇒ Number of **chairs** = 9 × 35 = 315

**∴ The correct answer is 315 chairs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

If a total quantity Q is divided in ratio a:b, then the first part is (a/(a+b)) × Q and the second part is (b/(a+b)) × Q.

Compound Ratio

For two ratios a:b and c:d, the compound ratio is (a × c) : (b × d).</p

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 59 and their product is 840. Find the sum of their squares.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **sum of squares** of two numbers is given by the formula: **(Sum)² − 2 × (Product)**.

⇒ Sum of squares = 59² − (2 × 840)

⇒ Sum of squares = 3481 − 1680

⇒ Sum of squares = 1801

**∴ The correct answer is 1801.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of two numbers (x + y) = 59

Product of the numbers (xy) = 840

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/29a8eb07c32a00502cc79bb501ca904c079234a07df31c2ecc16637f84f31d86.png] 

**Formula Used:**

We use the algebraic identity: **(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy**

**Calculations:**

⇒ (59)² = x² + y² + 2 × 840

⇒ 3481 = x² + y² + 1680

⇒ x² + y² = 3481 − 1680

⇒ x² + y² = 1801

**∴ The correct answer is 1801.**

**__Additional Information__**

Square of a Difference

The identity for the square of a difference is (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab. It can be related to the sum of squares as a² + b² = (a − b)² + 2ab.

Relationship between Identities

The two identities are linked by: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab. This is useful for finding the difference between numbers when the sum and product are known.

Difference of Two Squares

The formula a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b) is another fundamental identity used to factorize the difference of two quadratic terms.</p

questions.question: The average age of 16 students in a college is 20. Out of them, the average age of 5 students is 20 and the average age of the other 10 students is 20.4. Find the age of the 16th college student.
questions.solution:
**Given **

The average age of 16 student = 20 

the average age of 5 student = 20 

**Formula used **

Average = Sum of observation/No. of observation

**Calculation **

Total age of 16 student = 16 × 20 = 320 

⇒ Total age of 5 student = 5 × 20 = 100 

⇒ Total age of 10 student = 10 × 20.4 = 204 

⇒ Let the age of 16th student be x 

⇒ 320 = 100 + 204 + x 

⇒ x = 16 

**∴ The age of 16th college student is 16.**

questions.question: By selling an article for Rs 600, a shopkeeper makes a profit of 20%. At what price should he sell the article to incur a loss of 20% ?
questions.solution:
**Given **

Selling price of an article at 20% profit = Rs 600 

**Formula Used **

Cost price = selling price/(100 + profit%) × 100 

Selling price = cost price/100 × (100 - loss%)

**Calculation **

Cost price = (600/120) × 100 = Rs 500 

Selling price = (500/100) × 80 = Rs 400

**∴ The selling price of an article at 20% loss is Rs 400 **
